The community fix is die-stamped factory-gauge replacement panels rather than hand-formed patches: EDP-coated front and rear floor pans, rockers, wheelhouses and cowl repair sections (Key Parts/Quadratec, Classic 2 Current Fabrication) welded in after the rot is cut back to clean steel.
Any rust-through or heavily scaled structural metal should be cut back to solid steel and repaired with welded replacement floor pans, patch panels, or fabricated 16-18 gauge steel sections;
Evacuate, vacuum test for leaks, and recharge with R-1234yf.
Diagnose with scan tool to confirm actuator motor circuit fault.
For a misfire, follow the factory diagnostic path and use compression and leak-down results rather than assigning the code to the head.
Record the exact active and stored DTCs, follow the model-year circuit tree, and test the horn and steering-wheel functions independently before condemning the clockspring.

If circuit testing confirms the clockspring/steering-control assembly, select the replacement by VIN, model year, steering-wheel controls, steering-angle-sensor configuration, and current Mopar supersession.
Diagnose by elimination after CKP, fuel pump, and grounds are ruled out.
Fuel-pressure test before replacing.

If the vehicle or controller date is outside scope, the bulletin does not apply and the transmission complaint needs its normal diagnostic path.
For an in-scope vehicle, use the bulletin's P0868/gear-ratio decision path and compare desired, scan-reported actual, and mechanically measured line pressure with correct fluid level and temperature.
Diagnose before replacing parts.
Scan for transmission codes;
If the vehicle passes the test, do not replace PCV parts for this concern.
If the PCV system is correct, record a cylinder-compression test and perform a leak-down test using the applicable service specifications.
Also diagnose any visible external leak separately.
Do not order a PCV valve, revised hose, or catch can from oil use alone, and do not treat P052E or P0300 as part of this card without an actual scan and code-specific diagnosis.

Diagnose by pulling misfire codes on even-numbered (left-bank) cylinders and performing a leak-down/compression test;
Diagnose prerequisite five-volt-supply, throttle-position, accelerator-pedal, or other active faults in the order specified by the current factory procedure for that VIN and engine.

FCA's procedure is condition-dependent: a vehicle delivered in good running condition receives the campaign HPFP and associated non-contaminated-system service, while a non-running vehicle is diagnosed for pump failure and, when contamination is confirmed, receives the pump, in-tank modules, filters, injectors, rails, high-pressure tubes, fuel-system cleaning, and other campaign items specified for that vehicle.
Start with a complete vehicle scan and save active, stored, and environmental data before clearing anything.
Replace and VIN-configure a BCM, radio, IBS, or battery only when the component-specific test proves it failed.
Test both the main and auxiliary batteries;

If P0420/P0430 returns, exhaust restriction or loss of power remains, or other DTCs are present, continue with the current factory catalyst, fuel-control, misfire, exhaust-leak, and sensor diagnostics for the exact vehicle.
Read the ABS module and compare individual wheel-speed live data to isolate the affected circuit.
A battery test/replacement may be needed if the original was repeatedly deep-cycled.
Diagnose with a scan tool capable of reading hybrid control modules, then inspect for active recalls, battery pack faults, coolant heater issues, and software updates.
P0A0A, P0BBD, P1E15, U11E9
Perform a parasitic draw test with an ammeter and use a scan tool to identify modules staying awake;
Perform electrical pinpoint diagnostics from the sending unit through the Body Control Module to the cluster.
The accepted repair is replacing the fuel level sending unit (often supplied as part of the in-tank fuel pump/sender module), after which the gauge reads correctly.
Diagnose the failed actuator by circuit test/observation, then replace the affected blend-door actuator motor.
Diagnose whether noise originates at the PTU or the rear drive unit.
a broken shaft requires pulling the diff cover to retrieve the clip and inner stub.
Diagnosis usually starts by confirming loss of horn/cruise functions and scanning the airbag module for driver squib or clock spring circuit faults.
Diagnosis is based on repeat refueling shutoff/blowback behavior with no external filler obstruction.
Diagnose with a scan tool for sway-bar/4WD fault codes and inspect the actuator connector for green corrosion and water intrusion.
Diagnose in order of cost.
Replace steering stabilizer as part of death wobble diagnosis.
Test by idling with A/C on and confirming high-speed fan engagement.
If shifting faults persist, diagnose the valve body and shift solenoids;
Test the 12V auxiliary battery and charging system;
P0AA6, P1AF0, U0100
